hook: Why Does NASA Use 1990s Computer Chips in Mars Rovers? 🚀
headline: Why NASA Spacecraft Use 30-Year-Old 1990s Microprocessors
source: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory Avionics Specifications

slides.speaker: vr
slides.title: Old Tech in Space? 🛰️
slides.bubble: Wait, why is NASA using computer chips from the 1990s for Mars missions?

slides.speaker: vj
slides.title: Space Radiation Hazard ☢️
slides.bubble: Outer space is full of cosmic rays that mess with electronics. Think of them as tiny, powerful bullets.

slides.speaker: vr
slides.title: Modern Chip Vulnerability? 💡
slides.bubble: So, new, tiny chips would just... break? How so?

slides.speaker: vj
slides.title: Bit Flipping Explained 🔄
slides.bubble: Yes! Cosmic rays flip memory bits, causing errors or frying them completely. Modern chips are too sensitive.

slides.speaker: vr
slides.title: Rugged 1990s PowerPC ⚙️
slides.bubble: So NASA uses older, bigger chips? Like from my dad's old computer?

slides.speaker: vj
slides.title: Shielded for Survival 🛡️
slides.bubble: Exactly! They use robust 250nm chips, often with extra silicon shielding, built tough like tanks.

takeaway: Cosmic rays flip memory bits and fry modern 3nm chips in outer space. NASA uses rugged 250nm PowerPC chips from the 1990s wrapped in heavy silicon-on-insulator shields.
caption:
🤯 DID YOU KNOW? 🤯

Why are NASA's Mars rovers still running on 1990s computer chips?

It's not about budget cuts; it's about survival!

🔹 Space is full of high-energy cosmic rays.
🔹 These rays can flip memory bits or fry sensitive modern chips.
🔹 Older, larger 250nm chips (like PowerPC) are more resistant.
🔹 NASA uses these rugged chips, often with extra shielding, for reliability.
